persons.name: George Washington Dole
persons.note: TOWN TREASURER TWICE AND TRUSTEE TWICE - the most continuously documented office-holder in the dataset. Elected trustee 10 August 1833 with 26 of 28 votes (tied top of the poll with Owen), appointed town treasurer at the board's first business meeting on 4 September 1833, and elected trustee AND treasurer again at the third town election of July 1835 (Andreas, scan pp. 273, 369). He is therefore in office on the scene date on the face of the record. Also a provision packer: this dataset holds two slaughtering and packing buildings under his name. THE TOWN'S OWN ROLLS, 1833-1835 — CORROBORATION, NOT A GRADE. The early Chicago voter and tax lists held by the Illinois Regional Archives Depository name this person 3 times: Poll list of the first election of the Board of Trustees of the Town of Chicago, 10 August 1833 — “Dole, George W.” (poll_1833_010, line 31); Tax list of the Town of Chicago, 1833 — “Dole, George W.” (tax_1833_025, line 77); Election returns — poll list of 1834, filed 11 August 1834 — “Dole, George W.” (poll_1834_034, line 203). These are the town's own contemporary paper rather than a recollection of it, and each appearance says that a man of that name stood on that roll in that year — no more. The reading is twice mediated (Schulz's transcription, then Genealogy Trails' republication) and this project has not seen the IRAD originals. Under the ratified ladder (T-0513) the 1835 poll with a second independent source is attested, the 1835 poll alone or a 1833/1834 list with another source is inferred, and a single appearance with nothing else is a projected resident. This pass WRITES THE EVIDENCE AND MOVES NO GRADE — T-0515 applies the ladder against every source at once. Identity by the crosswalk's own rule: one resident of the surname 'Dole' agrees with the entry's forenames; 1 bearer(s) of the surname were considered. (data/research/civic/voter_crosswalk.json). FERGUS 1839'S LATER LISTS — 1837 AND 1839 EVIDENCE, NEVER AN 1835 FACT. Fergus' Chicago Directory for 1839 names this person 1 time in its two later lists: the city register of 1839 — “George W. Dole” as treasurer (f1839_r0005, printed page 38). What a match may carry, and it depends on WHICH TABLE it landed in. A match on printed page 38, or on any row of the mayors' table, is 1839-or-later evidence: it says the man held that office in that year and was therefore in Chicago in that year, it is written with the row's own describes_date and never as an 1835 fact, and the person's grade does not move on it alone — a later appearance is corroboration of CONTINUED RESIDENCE, not of July 1835. A match on the sheriffs' rows of 1831, 1832, 1834 or 1836 is different in kind: the office is contemporary with the town, the 1834 row's term covers the scene date outright, and such a match carries reaches_scene. Even there the SOURCE is a retrospect — a table running to 1874, set in 1876 out of Old Settlers' recollections per the compiler's warning on printed page 3 — so it may be cited as a contemporary office and may not be graded `documented` without a second, nearer record. The ward on printed page 38 is a ward of the CITY of 1839 and places no house in the town of 1835. Identity by the crosswalk's own rule: Surname 'Dole' folds to the same string as the register entry's, and the given name of both begins G. (data/research/directories/fergus_1839_election_crosswalk_1835.json and fergus_1839_register_crosswalk_1835.json). This pass WRITES THE EVIDENCE AND MOVES NO GRADE. citations.citation: The baptismal register of St Mary's, Chicago — the first Catholic parish in the town — opened by Father John Mary Irenaeus St. Cyr on 22 May 1833 and read here for the years 1833, 1834 and 1835: 57 entries in French and English naming children, parents, godparents and witnesses, with the priest's own signature under every one and eight autographs of the town's own people beside them.

transcribes.work: The baptismal register kept at Chicago by Father J. M. I. St. Cyr from May 1833
transcribes.note: THE ORIGINAL, and these eleven images are photographs of it. A reading made off them is scan_verified — the higher of this project's two reading grades — and it outranks the marriage and death pages of st_cyr_register_ichr_v4, which reached this project through a 1921-22 article and a web transcription.

what_it_supplies: 57 dated baptisms of 1833-1835 and 267 named readings of people — 46 of the entries at Chicago and 166 of the readings adults there
KINSHIP, which no other source this project holds gives at all: a child, its two parents and its two godparents on one dated line, 44 times over
the town's Catholic population — French, Métis, Irish and German — of whom 85 distinct adults reach no surname in the residents layer

eight AUTOGRAPHS: Mark Beaubien, Josette Laframboise, Augustin Bonné, Monique Nadeau, Jean Baptiste Lavigne, J. B. Beaubien, Robert A. Kinzie and Gwinthlean Whistler signing under the priest, each placing a named person at a named place on a named day in their own hand
two adult baptisms with AGES — Josette Laframboise Beaubien at 38 in June 1834 and Geneviève Medera at about 20 in June 1835 — which are the only ages this project has for either woman
the parish's own start date, 22 May 1833, on a page the book heads '1er Page'
the register's own arithmetic: pencil tallies of 19, 24 and 14 baptisms for 1833, 1834 and 1835, which check any reading of it
a hue and cry on the title page describing what a young man of the Illinois country wore in 1833 or 1834 — a white pea coat, gray pants and a fur cap
what_it_does_not_supply: any address, lot, street, dwelling or workplace — the register places nobody anywhere in the town, and names no church building on any of the eleven pages
residence, and this is the trap. A baptism documents a person at a font on a day. Presence is not residence and nothing here mints or regrades a resident
presence on 1 July 1835 for anyone not baptised or standing as sponsor within days of it
occupation. One entry writes 'Doctor Egan' — a title inside a name — and that is the only trade the book ever states

ALL CHICAGO. Entries 1-11 of 1834 were written at Bear Creek, the South Fork of the Sangamon and Springfield, in Sangamon County, on the priest's journey back from St. Louis. A reader who takes the book as a Chicago roll plants eleven households in the wrong county
reliable spelling. A French priest wrote Irish, English and German names and phoneticised Potawatomi and Odawa ones; the same woman is Nadeau, Nodeau and Nodou in his own hand on three pages
the sponsors of 1834 entry 4, which stood on a line the scan's frame cuts off
anything about 1836 or later. The two page-sides in the deposit that carry 1837-38 and 1849 entries are declared and not transcribed
